newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV CONTINUES WORLD CROSS DOMINANCE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV CONTINUES WORLD CROSS DOMINANCE.

text.p: Romania's Elena Fidatov continued her domination of the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) World Cross Challenge series by winning the 4.8 kilometres women's race on Sunday.
The 36 year-old Fidatov crossed the line in 15 minutes 50 seconds to record her sixth win of the series, but it was her hardest victory of the year.

She just held off Swiss teenager Anita Weyermann in a furious sprint over the final 200 metres of the treacherous course, which has drawn complaints from many top-class runners about its dangerous downhill slope.
Weyermann, the 1996 world junior 3,000 metres champion, finished second in 15:52 with South Africa's Colleen de Reuck third in 16:02.
Fidatov continues to lead the overall cross challenge rankings with 100 points. Ethiopia's Gete Wami, the reigning world champion, did not race on Sunday but remains second with 88 points.
Kenya's Bernard Barmasai narrowly beat Morocco's Mohammed Mourit in the 10.2 kilometres men's race for his second victory of the season.
Barmasai won in 30:41 compared with Mourit's second place time of 30:43.
Mourit is married to a Belgian and is hoping his Belgian citizenship will be processed in time to compete for his adopted country in next month's world cross country championships.
A distant third in the race was Germany's Dieter Baumann, the 1992 Olympic 5,000 metres champion, in 30:59.

Barmasai's win puts him in the lead in the men's world cross challenge standings with 72 points. Britain's Keith Cullen, who was the runner up earlier on Sunday in Chiba, Japan, stands second with 67 points.
The world cross challenge is a 12-race series and has a $25,000 first prize for both the men's and women's winners. The next race is Nairobi, Kenya on February 22.
